HEL-01.text: Revenue for fiscal 2026 rose 31% year over year to $2.84 billion, the fourth consecutive year of growth above 25%.

HEL-02.text: Operating margin expanded to 17.8% from 14.2% as module costs fell and the second automated assembly line reached full output.

HEL-03.text: Free cash flow turned positive at $212 million, compared with an outflow of $64 million in the prior year.

HEL-04.text: Net debt to EBITDA of 1.4x at year end, down from 2.3x a year earlier, with no covenant pressure on any facility.

HEL-05.text: Cash and undrawn credit lines total $640 million, equivalent to 34 months of runway at the current investment pace.

HEL-06.text: Contracted backlog reached a record $5.1 billion, roughly 1.8 times trailing revenue.

HEL-07.text: The largest customer accounted for 18% of revenue; no other customer exceeded 10%.

HEL-08.text: The shares trade at 19 times forward earnings, a discount to the sector median of 24 times despite faster growth.

HEL-09.text: The consensus price target of $48 implies about 22% upside from the current share price of $39.40.

HEL-10.text: Two brokers cut estimates in October citing weaker residential solar demand in Europe, trimming next-year growth forecasts to 22%.

HEL-11.text: Chinese module makers continue to cut prices; average selling prices fell 11% this year and management warned that further declines could compress margins.

HEL-12.text: A new patented cell architecture lifted module efficiency to 24.6%, about 1.5 points above the closest rival, and is already in volume production.

HEL-13.text: About 27% of FY2026 revenue depends on government tax-credit programs that legislators will review next year, creating policy uncertainty.

HEL-14.text: A fire at the Ohio cell plant in August halted output for three weeks; insurance is expected to cover most of the loss and production has fully resumed.

HEL-15.text: The stock fell as much as 26% from peak to trough over the past twelve months, a maximum drawdown that reflects high sensitivity to interest-rate expectations.

HEL-16.text: The chief executive sold 3% of her holdings under a pre-arranged trading plan in September.

judgement.rationale: Helios Renewables demonstrates strong financial performance with four consecutive years of revenue growth above 25% [HEL-01] and expanding operating margins [HEL-02]. The company has turned free cash flow positive and maintains a solid liquidity runway [HEL-03, HEL-05]. Furthermore, the stock trades at an attractive valuation discount to the sector median [HEL-08] with double-digit upside to consensus targets [HEL-09], easily outweighing the policy and competition risks cited by the bear case [HEL-13, HEL-11].
